framework.topicDescription: Assessment of how a company governs, understands, reduces, withstands, responds to and learns from physical-climate disruption and its cascading operational effects. Supersedes the 'Physical Climate Risk Management' framework: it keeps a dedicated physical-climate track while adding operational-resilience and performance tracks so that a mature business-continuity, crisis and recovery capability can be credited on its own terms without being mistaken for — or masking — physical-climate management.

antiInferenceRules: A general BCP, ERM, crisis-management or supplier-resilience disclosure may satisfy only a measure designated operational_resilience, and only when it meets that measure's named object/control/test gate.
General operational-resilience evidence does not by itself satisfy a physical_climate measure that requires physical hazard, climate scenario, physical-impact or climate-adaptation attribution.

A transition-risk, net-zero, emissions-reduction or renewable-energy disclosure does not satisfy a physical-climate measure unless the evidence independently identifies a physical hazard/impact and the required measure-specific control.
A climate/ESG statement does not satisfy an operational-resilience measure unless it describes the required continuity, recovery, dependency, crisis or exercise control.
A general policy, aspiration or outcome statement does not satisfy an implemented-control, test, decision-rule or performance measure without the required quote-verifiable tokens.
framework.scoringPersona: You are an expert physical-climate-resilience analyst. Your task is NOT to grade the quality of disclosure, but to assess how EFFECTIVELY a company reduces the exposure of its business to the damaging effects of climate change — through forward-looking strategic decisions (asset portfolio, siting, supply-chain strategy, capital allocation, insurability) and through responsiveness (business continuity, early warning, recovery and learning). Judge the substance of actions, decisions and outcomes against the physical-risk materiality the company plausibly faces for its sector, qualitatively. Reward named decisions, stated coverage and quantified outcomes; do not reward awareness, intent or process description on their own.

subAreaStructure.rationale: Recast from the five 'Physical Climate Risk Management' pillars into six resilience-and-continuity pillars that follow how a company understands, reduces, withstands, responds to and learns from physical-climate disruption and its cascading effects. The design follows IFRS S2's definition of climate resilience as strategic and operational capacity, and ISO 22301's managed business-continuity system, so that a mature, hazard-neutral continuity/recovery capability can be credited on an operational-resilience track without being mistaken for physical-climate management.

migration_27_to_36.note: Board oversight; broaden to physical-climate resilience but retain an explicit physical-risk link as the Yes requirement.
Executive accountability (G2, operational_resilience track, no pay linkage required) splits from incentive linkage (G3, a distinct differentiator).
Do not score policy existence alone: embedded decision controls (G5) split from technical design/maintenance standards (A3).
Replace the universal >=5-of-8 hazard-breadth rule with materiality-driven hazard selection and company-specific findings.
Retain long-horizon/high-warming analysis for long-lived assets; add an equally rigorous severe-physical-disruption stress route for asset-light businesses.
Retain explicit coverage; allow business-relevant denominators and implement a structured coverageRule (no 'all operations' inference).
Broaden beyond damage functions to business-consequence/financial-impact modelling; absorbs the forward-looking part of B6. Still reject exposure-only claims.
Supplier/logistics dependency mapping (U6) and shared infrastructure/utility/IT dependency mapping (U7) are distinct assessment objects.
Forward-looking physical-risk financial modelling -> U4; historic operational/financial impact measurement -> R2.
Gross-vs-residual exposed value becomes a strong supporting metric inside L1, not a standalone disclosure-format measure.
ERM integration; add risk appetite/tolerance or escalation threshold as the decision-control signal.
Expand from capex/site linkage to a plan with exposure linkage, ownership and dated milestones (asset-light routes allowed).
Allow capex, opex, staffing, reserves and contingency funding; remove the mandatory share-of-total-capex gate.
Retain completion + physical-risk-mechanism linkage; broaden covered population beyond sites with a deterministic coverage result.
Preserve the strategic bar; add business interruption, exclusions, deductibles and liquidity/residual-loss elements.
Technical future-climate design standards (A3) split from pre-commitment investment/siting due diligence (A4). Decision-embedding part -> G5.
Purpose unchanged but tightened at the boundary: asset hardening is A2; ownership/use/location/life/portfolio changes are A5.
Permit non-climate wording where it protects a named critical dependency; reject generic supplier-engagement language.
Merges with C10 into A11 (chronic-hazard operational continuity), conditional on material water/heat/smoke/workforce exposure.
Keep a defined appraisal requirement; allow business benefits beyond avoided loss.
Merges with C8 into A11; extends to chronic-condition effects on workforce safety and productive capacity.
A continuity system (P1), recovery objectives (P2), climate-scenario integration (P4) and exercised performance (P6) are scored independently.
Retain trigger-to-action requirement; broaden permitted hazard/dependency trigger classes.
Require recovery against an objective/service threshold rather than bare elapsed time; if_event_occurred applicability.
Retain quantification; remove the mandatory improving-trend condition.
Broaden targets to include risk tolerances and residual-exposure monitoring; require a baseline and current progress/status.
Include exercises and near misses so companies are not penalised for an absence of recent disasters.

measures.title: Board oversight of physical climate resilience is specific and active
measures.definition: Whether the board, or a named board committee, actively oversees physical climate resilience with an explicit physical-risk link and an evidenced depth signal. Replaces A1-board-oversight.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Score Yes only when all three predicates are quoted verbatim within the context window: a named board/committee, an explicit physical-climate-resilience remit, and one depth signal (cadence OR input OR decision). Generic 'the Board oversees climate-related risks', a committee name with no remit, or continuity oversight with no physical-risk connection is No. Do not infer depth from the existence of a committee alone.
measures.primaryAssessmentTarget: Board or named board committee's physical-climate-resilience oversight
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (requires explicit physical-climate / weather-hazard / physical-impact attribution). APPLICABILITY always for a public company (depth commensurate with exposure). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required for Yes: (1) names the board or a board committee; (2) explicitly links that body's remit to physical climate risk, climate resilience or named physical hazards (not generic 'climate-related risk' or ESG); and (3) shows ONE depth signal — a review cadence, a named information input, or a decision/change influenced by the oversight. Boundary: board-level oversight only here (executive ownership is G2; decision-embedding process is G5; independent review is G6). DEFINITION: a bounded disclosure must name the oversight body, tie it to physical climate risk, and evidence that the oversight is live through cadence, inputs or a decision — not a one-line governance claim.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A named board/committee with an explicit physical-climate remit AND a cadence, a named information input, or a documented decision driven by that oversight.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Generic 'the Board oversees climate-related risks' or ESG oversight with no physical specificity; a committee name with no remit; executive/management accountability with no board role (that is G2); a decision-embedding process (G5); internal audit/assurance review (G6); stakeholder-engagement statements.
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. An annual report or governance statement names the board/committee, states its physical-climate-resilience remit, and gives a review cadence (e.g. 'reviewed quarterly').
2. A proxy/governance disclosure names the committee and describes a specific physical-risk information input it receives (e.g. a physical-hazard exposure dashboard or scenario briefing).
3. A board minute, CDP governance answer or risk-report section records a board decision or change driven by physical-climate oversight (e.g. approving a resilience plan or deferring a site expansion on flood-risk grounds).
positiveExamples: The Risk Committee is responsible for physical climate risk and reviews a physical-hazard exposure dashboard at each quarterly meeting.
In 2025 the Board, on its Sustainability Committee's recommendation, deferred the Gulf Coast terminal expansion after a physical flood-risk review.
The Audit & Risk Committee's charter names oversight of climate-related physical hazards and receives a semi-annual resilience briefing from the Chief Risk Officer.
The Board reviewed the physical-climate scenario results in March and directed management to prioritise flood defences at the two highest-exposure plants.
negativeExamples: The Board maintains oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities as part of its ESG remit.
Our Sustainability Committee oversees the Group's net-zero transition and decarbonisation roadmap.
The Board is committed to building a resilient and sustainable business for all stakeholders.
Management holds primary responsibility for climate risk, reporting to the executive committee.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Generic climate/ESG oversight, an unremitted committee name, or management-only accountability with no board link.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A named board/committee with an explicit physical-climate-resilience remit and at least one live-oversight signal (cadence, specific input, or a decision it drove).
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Does the quote name the body, tie it to physical climate risk, AND show the oversight actually operating (not just existing)?

measures.title: Executive accountability and escalation for resilience are disclosed
measures.definition: Whether an accountable executive or management role owns resilience/continuity, with a defined responsibility and an escalation/reporting/resource mechanism. Replaces part of A2-exec-accountability-incentives (the accountability half; pay linkage is G3).
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a named accountable executive/role, a specific resilience/continuity/recovery responsibility, and an escalation/reporting/resource mechanism, all quote-verifiable. Naming a CSO/CRO/COO with no specific resilience mandate, or a generic executive committee, is No. Pay linkage is neither required nor sufficient here (that is G3).
measures.primaryAssessmentTarget: Executive ownership of resilience / continuity capability
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK operational_resilience (hazard-neutral: a named critical activity/dependency/disruption type plus a specific control/capability; climate wording is NOT required). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) names an accountable executive or management role; (2) defines that role's responsibility for resilience, continuity, emergency response or recovery; and (3) provides a reporting, escalation or resource-accountability mechanism. Boundary: executive ownership here; board oversight is G1; incentive/pay linkage is G3. DEFINITION: a disclosure must put a named role in charge of the resilience/continuity capability and show how issues escalate or how the role is resourced/held to account — not merely list a C-suite title.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A named executive/management role with a defined resilience/continuity/recovery responsibility and an escalation, reporting or resource-accountability mechanism.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A C-suite title with no specific resilience mandate; a generic 'the executive committee manages risk'; board-level oversight (G1); an incentive/remuneration link with no defined responsibility (G3); a policy with no named owner.
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. An annual report or policy names the executive/role accountable for business continuity or resilience and states a reporting line into senior management or the board.
2. A continuity/emergency-response policy assigns a named role responsibility for recovery and defines an escalation path for a major disruption.
3. A governance disclosure describes a management resilience committee chaired by a named executive with authority over resources or corrective actions.
positiveExamples: The Chief Operating Officer is accountable for the Group's operational resilience programme and reports quarterly to the Board Risk Committee.
Our Business Continuity Policy assigns the Head of Resilience responsibility for recovery and sets a defined escalation path to the Crisis Management Team for Tier-1 incidents.
A management Resilience Steering Group, chaired by the CRO, approves continuity resources and tracks remediation of exercise findings.
Divisional managing directors own continuity for their business units and escalate unresolved disruptions to the Group Operations Director within 24 hours.
negativeExamples: We have a strong risk-management culture led by our executive team.
The CEO is ultimately responsible for all risks facing the Group.
Our Chief Sustainability Officer leads our climate and ESG agenda.
Resilience is everyone's responsibility across the organisation.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A bare C-suite title, a generic committee, or 'everyone is responsible'.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A specific role owns resilience/continuity with a defined responsibility and an escalation or resource mechanism.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a named role, a specific continuity/recovery responsibility, AND a mechanism to escalate or resource it?

measures.title: Executive incentives link to a defined physical-resilience outcome
measures.definition: Whether a named executive remuneration or performance arrangement includes a defined resilience outcome/metric with a physical-climate link and a stated weighting or assessment mechanism. Replaces part of A2-exec-accountability-incentives (incentive half). This is a differentiator, not a gateway to crediting G2.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a named incentive arrangement, a defined resilience metric/outcome, an explicit physical-climate link, and a stated weighting/assessment mechanism. Generic ESG pay, net-zero/emissions-only incentives, or accountability with no incentive link is No. Do NOT credit G2 merely because G3 is met, and do not require G3 for G2.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (the incentivised outcome must carry a physical-climate / climate-adaptation / physical-hazard link). APPLICABILITY always (a company may demonstrate good accountability under G2 without disclosing pay linkage, so a No here is not a governance failure). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a named executive remuneration/performance arrangement; (2) a defined resilience outcome or metric within it; (3) a physical-climate / adaptation / physical-hazard link to that outcome; and (4) a stated weighting, target or assessment mechanism. DEFINITION: generic ESG pay or net-zero-only incentives do not qualify; the incentive must reward a physical-resilience or physical-adaptation result and show how it is weighted/assessed.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A named remuneration/performance arrangement with a defined resilience metric, an explicit physical-climate link, and a stated weighting/target/assessment mechanism.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Generic ESG or sustainability pay; net-zero or emissions-reduction incentives; a resilience 'consideration' with no metric or weighting; executive accountability with no incentive link (that is G2).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A remuneration report names a physical-resilience or adaptation metric in the executive scorecard with a stated percentage weighting.
2. A proxy statement ties a portion of the LTIP/annual bonus to a defined resilience target (e.g. completion of a site-hardening programme) with an assessment basis.
3. A governance disclosure states that executive variable pay is assessed partly against physical-climate adaptation milestones and describes how performance is measured.
positiveExamples: 20% of the CEO's annual scorecard is tied to delivery of the climate-resilience capital programme, assessed against site-hardening milestones.
The LTIP includes a physical-climate adaptation measure (weighting 10%) linked to flood-defence completion at the three highest-risk plants.
Executive bonuses are assessed partly against a drought-resilience water-reduction target at our water-stressed operations, with a defined threshold and stretch level.
The remuneration committee set a 15% weighting on business-interruption-days-avoided from the heat-resilience programme for operational executives.
negativeExamples: Executive remuneration includes an ESG modifier covering our broad sustainability agenda.
A portion of annual bonus is linked to progress on our net-zero emissions target.
The board considers climate performance when determining executive pay.
Our incentive plan rewards long-term value creation and responsible business.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Generic ESG pay, net-zero incentives, or no incentive link at all.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A named pay arrangement rewards a defined physical-resilience outcome with a stated weighting/assessment.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is the incentivised metric specifically a physical-resilience/adaptation outcome with a disclosed weighting, not a general ESG/emissions modifier?

measures.title: ERM prioritises physical climate risk with risk appetite or escalation thresholds
measures.definition: Whether physical climate risk or named physical hazards appear in ERM/risk reporting with a rating, materiality determination, risk appetite/tolerance or defined escalation threshold. Replaces B8-erm-integration-prioritisation.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires physical climate risk inside ERM PLUS at least one of: a rating/score, a materiality determination, a risk appetite/tolerance, or an escalation threshold, quote-verifiable. Climate named as an emerging issue with no ranking/threshold/action route is No.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (physical hazard/impact attribution required). APPLICABILITY always for a public company. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) physical climate risk or named physical hazards appear in the ERM/risk-management process or risk reporting; and (2) they are accompanied by a decision-control signal — a risk rating/score, a materiality determination, a risk appetite/tolerance statement, or a defined escalation threshold. Boundary: this is ERM prioritisation/appetite; board oversight is G1; embedding criteria into specific business decisions is G5. DEFINITION: climate merely listed as an 'emerging' or 'principal' risk with no ranking, threshold or action route does not qualify.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: Physical climate risk present in ERM/risk reporting with a rating, materiality determination, appetite/tolerance, or escalation threshold.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Climate listed as an emerging/principal risk with no rating, threshold or action route; a generic ERM framework with no physical-climate content (operational-resilience ERM alone belongs nowhere here); board oversight (G1); embedding into a specific decision type (G5).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A principal-risks table rates physical climate risk (likelihood/impact or a heat-map position) and states the treatment or owner.
2. A risk-management disclosure sets a risk appetite or tolerance statement that explicitly covers physical climate/weather risk.
3. An ERM description defines an escalation threshold (e.g. a loss or exposure trigger) at which physical-climate risk is escalated to a risk committee.
positiveExamples: Our principal-risks register rates physical climate risk as High/High and assigns it to the Group Risk Committee with a defined tolerance.
The Board has set a risk appetite that limits uninsured physical-climate loss exposure to 2% of EBITDA, triggering escalation above that level.
Physical climate hazards are scored in the enterprise risk heat map and breaching the amber threshold escalates to the Risk Committee.
Flood and heat risks carry a defined materiality rating in our ERM and are prioritised ahead of lower-rated risks for mitigation funding.
negativeExamples: Climate change is identified as an emerging risk in our risk universe.
We operate a comprehensive enterprise risk management framework aligned with ISO 31000.
Climate-related risks are considered as part of our principal risks and uncertainties.
Our risk appetite reflects our commitment to responsible and sustainable growth.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Climate named as an emerging risk with no ranking or threshold; a generic ERM framework.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: Physical climate risk is rated/prioritised in ERM or governed by an appetite/tolerance/escalation threshold.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Beyond listing climate as a risk, is there a rating, materiality call, appetite/tolerance, or escalation threshold attached to it?

measures.title: Material physical-risk and resilience criteria are embedded in business decisions
measures.definition: Whether a policy, process or approval rule requires a physical-risk/resilience assessment before a stated decision type, with a described criterion, threshold or approval consequence. Replaces part of A3-policy-framework and part of C5-siting-ma-design-standards (the decision-embedding part).
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a reusable decision-control process that mandates physical-risk/resilience assessment before a named decision type and states a criterion/threshold/approval consequence, all quote-verifiable. A generic 'we factor climate into decisions' or a one-off decision is No. Do not double-count with A3/A4/A5 unless the quote independently contains this gate.
measures.primaryAssessmentTarget: Decision-control process for capital allocation, projects, acquisitions, leases, outsourcing or material supplier selection
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (the embedded criterion must concern physical risk/resilience). APPLICABILITY if_material — for companies that make material capital, project, acquisition, lease, outsourcing or supplier-selection decisions (most operating companies). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a reusable policy/process/approval rule (not a one-off); (2) it requires a physical-risk/resilience assessment BEFORE a stated decision type; and (3) it describes a criterion, threshold or approval consequence. Boundary: this is the decision GATE/process; the technical design standard applied is A3; pre-commitment due-diligence screening is A4; portfolio decisions are A5. DEFINITION: a generic commitment to 'consider climate in decisions', or a single past decision with no reusable process, is No.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A reusable policy/process/approval rule requiring a physical-risk/resilience assessment before a stated decision type, with a criterion, threshold or approval consequence.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A generic commitment to consider climate in decisions; a one-off decision with no reusable process; policy existence with no decision gate; the technical design standard itself (A3); pre-commitment site/asset screening (A4); portfolio relocation/retirement decisions (A5).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A capital-approval or investment policy requires a physical-risk assessment before project sign-off and states an approval consequence (e.g. escalation or rejection above a risk threshold).
2. A procurement/outsourcing standard requires physical-resilience due diligence before selecting a critical supplier or site, with a defined criterion.
3. An M&A/leasing policy mandates a physical-climate screening step in the approval workflow and specifies the threshold at which the decision is escalated.
positiveExamples: Our capital-approval framework requires a physical-climate risk assessment for any project above £10m; projects exceeding the risk threshold require Board Risk Committee approval.
The procurement standard mandates a physical-resilience due-diligence check before onboarding any single-source critical supplier.
Site-selection policy requires a flood- and heat-exposure assessment prior to lease commitment, and locations above the defined risk band are rejected or escalated.
Our M&A playbook includes a mandatory physical-climate screening gate before completion, with findings fed into the valuation and approval decision.
negativeExamples: We take climate change into account in our investment decisions.
Sustainability is embedded across everything we do.
The Group approved a new flood barrier at its Rotterdam site last year.
Our capital allocation prioritises long-term value creation.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A generic 'we consider climate', or a single past decision with no process.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A reusable approval process requires a physical-risk assessment before a named decision type and defines a criterion/threshold/consequence.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a repeatable decision rule with a physical-risk gate and a stated consequence, not just awareness or one example?

measures.title: Resilience-control effectiveness receives independent review or formal management review
measures.definition: Whether internal audit, assurance, board review or a formal management review evaluates resilience/continuity control effectiveness, identifies findings, or records a review cycle and corrective actions. New measure (no single legacy equivalent).
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires an independent/formal review that tests resilience-control effectiveness and produces findings or a review-cycle-plus-corrective-actions record, quote-verifiable. Self-certification or unevaluated policy approval is No.
measures.primaryAssessmentTarget: Challenge and review of resilience controls
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (the reviewed controls are the physical-climate-resilience/continuity controls). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) an independent or formal review body/process — internal audit, external assurance, board review or a formal management review; (2) it evaluates the EFFECTIVENESS of resilience/continuity controls (not merely their existence); and (3) it identifies findings, or records a review cycle AND corrective actions. Boundary: this is challenge/assurance of control effectiveness; board oversight of the risk is G1; the ERM rating is G4. DEFINITION: self-certification, or a policy 'approved' with no evidence of evaluation, is No.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: An independent or formal review (internal audit, assurance, board or formal management review) of resilience-control effectiveness that identifies findings or records a review cycle with corrective actions.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Self-certification; a policy 'reviewed and approved' with no evaluation of effectiveness; board oversight of the risk itself (G1); the ERM risk rating (G4); an exercise/test of continuity arrangements (that is P6).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. An internal-audit or assurance report evaluates the continuity/resilience control framework and lists findings and remediation actions.
2. A governance disclosure records a formal management review of resilience-control effectiveness on a stated cycle, with corrective actions tracked to closure.
3. A board/committee record documents an independent review of the resilience programme's effectiveness and the resulting improvement actions.
positiveExamples: Internal Audit completed an assurance review of the Group's physical-climate resilience and business-continuity controls in 2025, raising four findings now tracked to closure.
The physical-climate resilience programme is subject to a formal annual management review that assesses control effectiveness and assigns corrective actions.
An independent third party assured our continuity management system, covering our flood and extreme-weather response, against ISO 22301 and identified two non-conformities with agreed remediation.
The Board Risk Committee reviewed the effectiveness of physical-climate resilience controls and directed improvements to the escalation process.
negativeExamples: Our business-continuity policy is reviewed and approved annually by management.
We maintain robust internal controls across the organisation.
The Board is satisfied that the Group's risk-management arrangements are effective.
We are committed to continuous improvement in our resilience capabilities.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Self-certification, or policy approval with no evaluation of whether controls work.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: An independent/formal review tests resilience-control effectiveness and yields findings or a review cycle plus corrective actions.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is the effectiveness of the controls actually evaluated (with findings/actions), rather than the policy merely being approved?

measures.title: Material physical hazards are assessed with company-specific findings
measures.definition: Whether the company identifies the physical hazards relevant to its footprint/business model and discloses a company-specific result for each relevant hazard class assessed. Replaces B1-hazard-coverage. CRITICAL-GATE measure (criticalMeasureSet).
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires materially-relevant hazards identified AND at least one company-specific finding per relevant hazard class (location, operational implication, or materiality rationale). Do NOT require a fixed number of hazards. A generic list of climate hazards with no company-specific result is No. Treat a U1 No as a critical-gate failure in narrative.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (explicit hazard/physical-impact attribution required). APPLICABILITY always for a public company; evidence depth commensurate with exposure. CRITICAL GATE: U1 is one of the four criticalMeasureSet measures [U1, U2, A1, P4] — in the deferred weighted model a failed critical measure caps the rating (CoreGate); encoded here so a reviewer treats a U1 failure as materially serious. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) identifies physical hazards RELEVANT to the company's footprint/business model (materiality-driven, not a fixed breadth count); and (2) discloses, for each relevant hazard class assessed, a company-specific finding — an affected location, an operational implication, or a materiality rationale. CHANGE FROM LEGACY: the universal '>=5 of 8 hazards' rule is REMOVED; a geographically concentrated company with a genuinely narrow risk profile must not be penalised. DEFINITION: require relevance plus company-specific results, not generic hazard breadth.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: Materially-relevant physical hazards identified with company-specific findings (affected locations, operational implications, or materiality rationale) for each relevant hazard class.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A generic catalogue of climate hazards with no company-specific result; 'climate change may affect our operations'; a hazard map purchased with no interpretation; exposure screening coverage (that is U2); vulnerability/consequence method (that is U4).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A TCFD/CDP or annual-report disclosure lists the hazards material to the company and states, for each, the affected sites/regions or the operational consequence identified.
2. A risk disclosure explains why a given hazard is (or is not) material to the business model and gives the company-specific finding that supports it.
3. A sustainability report presents a hazard-by-hazard assessment result for the company's own operations (not a generic hazard primer).
positiveExamples: We assessed flood, extreme-heat and water-stress exposure; 12 of our 40 sites lie in high flood-risk zones, chiefly in South-East Asia.
Wildfire is our dominant physical hazard: three Californian facilities face elevated risk, while our northern-European sites are immaterial for wildfire.
As a single-campus software firm, our material physical hazard is heat/grid stress at our Phoenix data centre; coastal and wildfire hazards are not material to us.
Drought and river-flooding were each assessed; drought materially affects two water-intensive plants in Spain, with quantified production-at-risk.
negativeExamples: Climate change presents a range of physical risks to businesses globally.
We recognise that extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and severe.
The Group is exposed to acute and chronic climate hazards across its value chain.
We purchased a climate hazard dataset covering all major perils.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Generic hazard lists, bought hazard maps, or 'climate may affect us' with no company result.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: Relevant hazards identified with company-specific findings per hazard class (locations/consequences/materiality).
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Does the company state its OWN findings for each relevant hazard, rather than describing hazards in general?

measures.title: Material exposure screening has a stated, appropriate coverage denominator
measures.definition: Whether the disclosure identifies the screened population, gives a stated coverage figure or complete enumerated population, and covers at least the applicable threshold of material exposure. Replaces B3-asset-screening-coverage. CRITICAL-GATE measure.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a defined population, a STATED coverage figure (numerator/denominator) or a complete enumerated population, and coverage at/above the applicable threshold, all quote-verifiable. 'Across our operations', 'company-wide' or 'all sites' with no figure or enumeration is No. Accepted denominators include sites, facilities, asset value, revenue and production capacity.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (physical-exposure attribution required). APPLICABILITY always. CRITICAL GATE (criticalMeasureSet [U1,U2,A1,P4]). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) physical-climate attribution of the screening; (2) a defined population of material exposure (sites, assets, revenue, production capacity, insured value or equivalent); (3) a stated coverage numerator/denominator OR a complete enumerated population; and (4) coverage meets the applicable threshold policy (default 0.50, materiality-adjusted). CHANGE FROM LEGACY: coverage may NOT be inferred from 'all operations'; it needs a structured coverage rule (see coverageRule). DEFINITION: a quantified or fully-enumerated coverage of a defined material population, on a business-relevant denominator — not a vague 'company-wide' claim.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A defined material population with a stated coverage numerator/denominator or a complete enumeration, on a business-relevant denominator, at/above the applicable threshold.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: 'Across our operations' / 'company-wide' / 'all sites' with no figure or enumeration; coverage inferred from a general statement; hazard identification without a coverage denominator (that is U1); vulnerability method (U4).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure states a coverage ratio over a defined population (e.g. '310 of 356 facilities screened for physical climate risk').
2. A disclosure gives a percentage on a business-relevant denominator (e.g. '82% of asset value assessed for flood and heat exposure').
3. A disclosure enumerates the complete material population and confirms all were screened (e.g. 'all 14 material plants assessed').
positiveExamples: We screened 310 of 356 facilities (87%) for physical climate exposure, covering all sites above our materiality threshold.
82% of asset value and 100% of our top-20 revenue-generating sites were assessed for flood, heat and water-stress exposure.
All 14 material manufacturing plants were enumerated and individually screened for acute and chronic physical hazards.
Physical-risk screening covered 75% of insured property value, with the remaining low-value leased offices excluded as immaterial and the rationale stated.
negativeExamples: We assess physical climate risk across our operations.
Our climate risk screening covers the whole Group.
All material sites are reviewed for climate-related risks.
We have conducted a company-wide climate risk assessment.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: 'All operations'/'company-wide' with no figure, or inferred coverage.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A stated coverage ratio or complete enumeration over a defined material population on a business denominator, meeting threshold.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a numerator/denominator or a complete named population — not just a claim that everything is covered?

measures.title: Scenario or stress analysis is commensurate with business exposure and planning horizons
measures.definition: Whether the company uses a physical-climate scenario or severe physical-disruption stress, states an appropriate horizon, and links it to asset life, contracts, strategic plan, exposure or a decision process. Replaces B2-scenario-horizons.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a physical-climate scenario or severe physical-disruption stress, an appropriate stated horizon, and a link to asset life/contracts/strategy/exposure/decisions, quote-verifiable. A named scenario with no horizon or no decision linkage is No. Do not force a >2050 high-warming horizon on asset-light businesses if a severe decision-relevant stress is disclosed.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate. APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a physical-climate scenario OR a severe physical-disruption stress test; (2) a stated, appropriate horizon; and (3) a link from the exercise to asset life, contracts, strategic plan, exposure or a decision process. CHANGE FROM LEGACY: a high-warming scenario beyond 2050 remains a strong route for long-lived-asset owners but is NOT a universal gate; asset-light/service/short-cycle businesses may qualify via another severe, decision-relevant physical-disruption analysis. DEFINITION: the analysis must be decision-relevant and horizon-appropriate to THIS company, not a generic scenario mention.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A physical-climate scenario or severe physical-disruption stress, with an appropriate stated horizon, linked to asset life, contracts, strategy, exposure or a decision.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A scenario named with no horizon; a horizon with no decision/exposure link; a transition-only (net-zero/2°C emissions-pathway) scenario with no physical-impact analysis; exposure screening (U2); correlated/cascading analysis (U8).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A long-lived-asset owner runs a high-warming physical scenario to 2050+ and links results to asset life/capex planning.
2. An asset-light firm stress-tests a severe multi-week outage of a critical data-centre region and links it to its continuity/strategic plan over a relevant horizon.
3. A disclosure states the scenario(s), the horizon chosen and why it fits the business, and the decision or plan the results informed.
positiveExamples: We ran RCP8.5 to 2050 and 2080 across our property portfolio and used the results to set the asset-life and capex plan for coastal sites.
As an asset-light payments firm we stress-tested a 10-day loss of our primary cloud region to extreme heat; results fed our continuity strategy over a 3-year horizon.
Physical-climate scenarios at 2030 and 2050 were linked to lease-renewal decisions for our highest-exposure distribution centres.
A severe drought stress over a 5-year horizon was modelled for our beverage operations and informed the water-resilience investment plan.
negativeExamples: We consider a range of climate scenarios in our strategy.
Our analysis is aligned with a 1.5°C transition pathway and net-zero by 2050.
We use RCP scenarios published by the IPCC.
Climate scenario analysis is an area of ongoing development for the Group.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A named scenario with no horizon or no decision link; a transition-only emissions scenario.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A physical scenario/stress with an appropriate horizon linked to asset life, contracts, strategy, exposure or a decision.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is a PHYSICAL scenario/stress run at a horizon that fits the business AND tied to a decision, not just named?

measures.title: Vulnerability and business consequences are assessed, not only hazard exposure
measures.definition: Whether the company describes a method linking a physical hazard/exposure to vulnerability or consequence (asset sensitivity, damage function, design threshold, downtime/production model, revenue/cash-flow impact, service interruption or customer consequence). Replaces B4-vulnerability-methodology and the forward-looking part of B6-financial-impact.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a described method linking hazard/exposure to a vulnerability or business consequence, quote-verifiable. Hazard maps, vendor names, or a loss estimate with no stated basis/method are No. Forward-looking only — realised event losses are R2.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate. APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a physical hazard/exposure input; and (2) a described METHOD that links it to vulnerability or business consequence — asset sensitivity, damage function, design threshold, downtime/production model, revenue/cash-flow impact, service interruption or customer consequence. Boundary: this is forward-looking consequence METHOD; historic realised incident impact is R2; hazard identification is U1. DEFINITION: reject exposure-only outputs — a hazard map, a vendor name, or a loss figure with no stated basis/method does not qualify.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A described method linking physical hazard/exposure to vulnerability or business/financial consequence (damage function, sensitivity, downtime/production model, revenue/cash-flow impact, service/customer consequence).
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A hazard/exposure map with no consequence method; a vendor/tool name alone; a loss number with no stated basis; historic realised event losses (R2); hazard identification only (U1).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure describes damage functions or asset-sensitivity curves applied to exposed assets to estimate expected damage/downtime.
2. A disclosure models revenue/cash-flow or production impact from a hazard using a stated methodology and assumptions.
3. A disclosure links a design threshold or service-interruption model to a quantified or bounded business consequence.
positiveExamples: We apply asset-specific damage functions to flood depth to estimate expected annual damage and downtime per facility.
Our model translates heat-days above 40°C into productivity loss and cooling-cost impact for outdoor operations, with stated assumptions.
A cash-flow-at-risk method links drought severity to production curtailment and revenue impact at our two water-intensive plants.
We model service-interruption hours from storm scenarios and the resulting customer-SLA and revenue consequences for our network.
negativeExamples: We use Munich Re's climate risk data to assess exposure.
Our assets face increasing risk from floods and storms.
We estimate potential climate losses of up to $50m (no basis disclosed).
Hazard maps show several sites in high-risk zones.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Exposure maps, vendor names, or a loss figure with no method; realised event losses.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A described method converting hazard/exposure into vulnerability or business/financial consequence.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a stated METHOD linking hazard to consequence, forward-looking, rather than exposure or an unexplained number?

measures.title: Critical business activities and tolerable disruption are defined
measures.definition: Whether the company identifies critical activities, products, services or systems and discloses a bounded tolerable-disruption parameter (maximum tolerable disruption, RTO, RPO, criticality ranking or equivalent). New measure (no legacy equivalent).
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires named critical activities AND a bounded disruption/recovery parameter (MTD/RTO/RPO/criticality ranking), quote-verifiable. 'We have performed a business impact analysis' with no critical activity or parameter is No.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK operational_resilience (hazard-neutral: a named critical activity plus a bounded prioritisation; climate wording NOT required). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) identifies critical activities, products, services or systems; and (2) discloses a bounded tolerable-disruption parameter — maximum tolerable disruption/downtime, recovery-time objective (RTO), recovery-point objective (RPO), criticality ranking or equivalent. Boundary: this is the BIA/prioritisation; recovery STRATEGY and objectives are P2; the continuity SYSTEM is P1. DEFINITION: a generic BIA/continuity claim with no named critical activity or recovery parameter does not qualify.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: Named critical activities/products/services/systems with a bounded tolerable-disruption parameter (MTD, RTO, RPO, criticality ranking or equivalent).
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A generic 'we conduct a BIA'/'we have continuity plans' with no named critical activity or recovery parameter; recovery strategy/objectives detail (P2); the continuity system itself (P1); dependency mapping (U6/U7).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure names its critical activities/systems and states a maximum tolerable disruption or RTO for each tier.
2. A disclosure presents a criticality ranking of products/services with recovery priorities.
3. A disclosure states RPO/RTO targets for critical systems identified in its BIA.
positiveExamples: Our BIA identifies order-processing and payments as Tier-1 activities with a maximum tolerable downtime of 4 hours.
We rank our 9 critical services and set RTOs ranging from 2 to 24 hours by criticality tier.
Critical systems carry defined RPOs (data loss tolerance) of 15 minutes for transactional platforms.
The business-impact analysis designates three production lines as critical, each with a stated tolerable interruption window.
negativeExamples: We perform regular business impact analyses across the Group.
Business continuity is embedded in our operations.
We understand which parts of our business are most important.
Our continuity plans ensure we can keep operating.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A generic BIA/continuity claim with no critical activity or parameter.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: Named critical activities/systems with a bounded disruption/recovery parameter.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Are specific critical activities named AND bounded by MTD/RTO/RPO/criticality — not just a claim that a BIA exists?

measures.title: Critical supplier and logistics dependencies are mapped and prioritised
measures.definition: Whether the company identifies critical supplier, input, route, inventory or logistics dependencies and states a coverage, criticality ranking, single-source concentration, or priority population. Replaces part of B5-valuechain-infra-exposure.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires named critical supplier/logistics dependencies AND a coverage/ranking/concentration/priority population, quote-verifiable. Generic 'supply chains face disruption risk' or actions with no dependency assessment is No. Supplier ACTIONS are A8; infrastructure dependencies are U7.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK operational_resilience (named critical dependency + prioritisation; climate wording NOT required). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) identifies critical supplier/input/route/inventory/logistics dependencies; and (2) states a coverage, criticality ranking, single-source concentration, or priority population. Boundary: this is dependency MAPPING; the resilience ACTION on those dependencies is A8; infrastructure/utility/IT dependencies are U7. DEFINITION: generic supply-chain-disruption language, or supplier resilience ACTIONS with no evidence of dependency assessment, does not qualify.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: Named critical supplier/input/route/inventory/logistics dependencies with a coverage, criticality ranking, single-source concentration, or priority population.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Generic supply-chain-disruption risk language; supplier resilience ACTIONS with no dependency assessment (that is A8); infrastructure/utility/IT dependencies (U7); a supplier code of conduct.
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure maps critical suppliers/inputs and states single-source concentration or a tier-1 criticality ranking.
2. A disclosure identifies key logistics routes/nodes and a priority population (e.g. 'top 20 suppliers by criticality').
3. A disclosure states coverage of its supplier base assessed for dependency criticality.

Our logistics dependency assessment identifies three port nodes whose disruption would halt 60% of outbound volume.
Critical-input dependency mapping covers 85% of direct spend and ranks suppliers by criticality tier.
We identified two sole-source active-ingredient suppliers as our highest supply-chain dependency concentration.
negativeExamples: We work closely with our suppliers to manage risk.
Supply chain disruption is a risk we monitor.
We have a diverse global supplier base.
Our procurement team ensures resilient sourcing.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Generic supply-chain risk language, or actions with no dependency assessment.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: Named critical supplier/logistics dependencies with coverage/ranking/concentration/priority population.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a mapped/prioritised set of critical supplier-logistics dependencies — not just engagement or an action?

measures.title: Critical infrastructure, utility and technology dependencies are mapped and prioritised
measures.definition: Whether the company names a material infrastructure/utility/technology dependency class, its service/operational relevance, and a coverage, ranking, vulnerability or recovery requirement. Replaces part of B5-valuechain-infra-exposure.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a named infrastructure/utility/tech dependency class, its operational relevance, AND a coverage/ranking/vulnerability/recovery requirement, quote-verifiable. 'We rely on power and IT' with no relevance or prioritisation is No. Controls are A9; supplier dependencies are U6.
measures.primaryAssessmentTarget: Dependencies on power, water, telecoms, transport, data/IT, communications or other enabling infrastructure

measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A named infrastructure/utility/technology dependency class with stated operational relevance and a coverage, ranking, vulnerability or recovery requirement.

Telecoms and transport corridors feeding our distribution hub were mapped and prioritised by operational criticality.

Power and connectivity are important to our business.
We have backup generators at our head office.
Our operations rely on third-party utilities and networks.

measures.title: Correlated and cascading disruption is assessed
measures.definition: Whether a physical hazard or scenario is analysed for its ability to disrupt more than one relevant operation, facility, supplier, utility, transport corridor or service at the same time, with a stated dependency or consequence. New measure (no legacy equivalent).
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a physical hazard/scenario analysed for simultaneous/correlated disruption across more than one dependency, with a stated consequence, quote-verifiable. Independent single-asset analyses do not qualify unless their correlation is analysed.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate. APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a physical hazard or scenario; (2) analysed for SIMULTANEOUS disruption of MORE THAN ONE relevant operation, facility, supplier, utility, transport corridor or service; and (3) a stated dependency or consequence of that correlated failure. Boundary: single-asset hazard analysis is U1/U4; this measure requires correlation/cascade. DEFINITION: one-asset hazard analysis that does not consider correlated failure does not qualify.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A physical hazard/scenario analysed for simultaneous disruption of more than one operation/facility/supplier/utility/route/service, with a stated dependency or consequence.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Single-asset hazard analysis (U1/U4); independent per-site assessments with no correlation; a generic statement that risks are 'interconnected'; dependency mapping with no hazard-driven correlation (U6/U7).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure analyses how one storm/flood event would simultaneously hit multiple sites in a region plus a shared supplier or port.
2. A scenario examines concurrent heat-driven grid failure and water-supply loss across co-located operations.

measures.category: Reduce vulnerability and adapt the business
measures.title: A physical-climate adaptation/resilience plan has owners, milestones and exposure linkage
measures.definition: Whether a disclosed plan identifies an adaptation action portfolio, links it to material physical exposure/hazards, names owners or governance, and includes dated milestones, budget/action status or a decision timetable. Replaces C1-adaptation-strategy. CRITICAL-GATE measure.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires all four predicates quote-verifiable: an action portfolio, physical-exposure linkage, named ownership/governance, and a dated milestone / action status / decision timetable. A statement of intent, a resilience 'ambition' with no owner or date, or a plan with no physical-exposure link is No. Operating-model / supplier / technology adaptation routes are accepted — do not require capex.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (explicit physical-climate / hazard attribution required). APPLICABILITY always. CRITICAL GATE (criticalMeasureSet [U1,U2,A1,P4]). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required for Yes: (1) an identified adaptation/resilience ACTION portfolio (not an aspiration); (2) an explicit link to material physical exposure or named hazards; (3) a named owner or governance accountability for the plan; and (4) a dated milestone, budget/action status, or a decision timetable. CHANGE FROM LEGACY: capex/site-plan linkage is a VALID route, not the only route — asset-light businesses may adapt through operating models, supplier arrangements or technology/hosting choices, and those count. Boundary: a PLAN with owners+milestones here; a completed/operational control is A2; resourcing amounts are A6; appraisal basis is A7. DEFINITION: a bounded disclosure must show an owned, time-bound adaptation plan tied to the company's own physical exposure — not a generic commitment to 'build resilience'.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: An owned, dated adaptation action plan (capex OR operating-model/supplier/technology route) explicitly linked to the company's material physical exposure.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A generic 'we are building climate resilience' ambition; a plan with no owner or no date; an adaptation goal with no link to the company's own physical exposure; a completed single control (A2); a resourcing figure alone (A6); an appraisal method alone (A7).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report sets out an adaptation plan with named workstreams tied to the company's flood/heat/water exposure, a responsible owner, and dated milestones to 2027.
2. An asset-light firm discloses a resilience plan to re-architect hosting across climate-resilient regions, owned by the COO, with a phased timetable and status per phase.
3. A CDP/TCFD disclosure links an adaptation action portfolio to material hazard findings, names the accountable committee, and reports budget allocated and percentage complete.
positiveExamples: Our Climate Adaptation Plan sets five workstreams addressing our flood- and heat-exposed sites, is owned by the Group Resilience Director, and has dated milestones through 2027 with status reported quarterly.

As an asset-light business we are migrating critical workloads to three climate-resilient hosting regions; the programme is owned by the COO with a phased 2025-2026 timetable and completion status per region.

The Board-approved adaptation portfolio links each action to a material physical hazard identified in our screening, names an accountable owner per action, and allocates GBP 40m across a three-year milestone plan.

Our resilience roadmap ties supplier-diversification and inventory-buffering actions to drought and flood exposure in our sourcing regions, with the Chief Procurement Officer accountable and target dates for each action.
negativeExamples: We are committed to building resilience to climate change across our business.
The company recognises the importance of adapting to physical climate risks.
We have an ambition to make our operations more climate-resilient over time.
A climate adaptation strategy is under development and will be published in due course.

measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A future/planned action; an isolated pilot with no materiality or coverage; a generic environmental or emissions action; an asset ownership/use/location change (that is A5); a plan with owners/milestones (A1).

During 2025 we commissioned backup water-storage and recycling at all four drought-exposed manufacturing sites, cutting mains dependency by 60%.
Wildfire defensible-space and ember-resistant retrofits were completed at the three facilities within our highest-rated fire zones.

measures.title: Engineering, maintenance and design standards apply future resilience thresholds where material
measures.definition: Whether a standard or rule specifies a future-relevant climate/design threshold or requirement and identifies the assets/project classes to which it applies. Replaces part of A3-policy-framework and C5-siting-ma-design-standards.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a standard/rule, a future-relevant climate/design threshold, and a defined asset/project-class scope, all quote-verifiable. measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (future-climate/design threshold attribution required). APPLICABILITY if_material (applies where the company has physical assets, facilities or capital projects whose design/maintenance can embed climate thresholds; non-applicable for pure asset-light models with no design control — handled as an applicability determination, not an automatic No). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a standard, rule or specification exists; (2) it specifies a FUTURE-relevant climate/design threshold, return period, or heat/wind/flood/water/fire requirement (not historical code compliance alone); and (3) it identifies the assets or project classes to which it applies. Boundary: technical DESIGN/maintenance thresholds here; pre-commitment due-diligence screening is A4; embedding into governance/decision process is G5. DEFINITION: a technical requirement with a forward-looking climate threshold and a defined scope of application — not a policy statement with no technical content.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A technical standard/rule with a forward-looking climate/design threshold and a defined set of assets or project classes it governs.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Historical building-code compliance alone; a policy with no technical/operational requirement; a general design-quality statement; pre-commitment site screening (A4); decision-process embedding (G5).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:

Data-centre and logistics projects must meet design wet-bulb and peak-wind thresholds aligned to 2050 climate scenarios under our Group Technical Standard.
The estate maintenance standard mandates drainage and roof upgrades to projected rainfall-intensity return periods for all owned warehouses.
Our design code specifies climate-adjusted cooling-capacity margins for all critical plant procured after 2024.
negativeExamples: All our buildings comply with local building codes and regulations.
We maintain high standards of engineering and design quality.
The company follows good practice in facilities management.
We aim to design resilient infrastructure across our estate.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Historical code compliance only, or a policy with no technical requirement.

c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Does the standard set a FUTURE climate threshold and say which assets/projects it governs — beyond current-code compliance?

measures.category: Reduce vulnerability and adapt the business
measures.title: Physical risk is assessed before committing to material locations, acquisitions, leases, outsourcing or critical suppliers
measures.definition: Whether a disclosed process requires physical-risk due diligence before at least one specified commitment type, plus a decision criterion or escalation/approval consequence. Replaces part of C5-siting-ma-design-standards.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a process, a named pre-commitment type, and a decision/escalation consequence, all quote-verifiable. measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (physical-risk due-diligence attribution required). APPLICABILITY if_material (applies where the company makes material commitment decisions — new locations, M&A, leases, outsourcing, supplier onboarding). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a disclosed PROCESS requiring physical-risk due diligence; (2) it applies BEFORE at least one specified commitment type (location, acquisition, lease, outsourcing or critical supplier); and (3) it carries a decision criterion or an escalation/approval consequence. DEFINITION: a gate in the company's commitment process that forces physical-risk assessment before a decision and can change it — not a general responsible-investment statement.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A process requiring physical-risk assessment before a named commitment type, with a decision criterion or escalation/approval consequence.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Retrospective screening of existing sites (that is U1/U2); a general responsible-investment or ESG due-diligence statement; a screening that cannot affect the decision; technical design standards (A3).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure states physical-climate due diligence is mandatory before any site acquisition or major lease, with sign-off required from the Risk Committee.
2. An M&A process requires a physical-risk assessment of target assets, and material findings must be escalated to the investment committee before approval.

Critical new suppliers must pass physical-hazard screening during onboarding; high-risk results require mitigation plans or disqualify the supplier.
Before approving a new outsourced data-centre region, our process requires a physical-climate exposure review and a documented go/no-go decision.
negativeExamples: We take environmental factors into account in our investment decisions.
The company conducts due diligence on acquisitions in line with good practice.
We screen our existing sites for physical climate risk annually.
Responsible investment principles guide our capital allocation.

c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A pre-commitment process forcing physical-risk assessment before a named decision type, with a decision/escalation consequence.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Does physical-risk assessment happen BEFORE a commitment and can it change the decision?

measures.definition: Whether the company discloses an actual or defined decision pathway to relocate, retire, sell, redesign, harden or otherwise alter material high-risk assets, with the physical-risk rationale and a decision status or portfolio coverage. Replaces C6-asset-portfolio-decisions.

measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (physical-risk rationale required). APPLICABILITY if_material (applies where the company holds a material portfolio of physical assets exposed to climate hazards). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) an actual decision OR a defined decision pathway affecting material high-risk assets (relocate, retire, sell, redesign, harden or alter use/life/allocation); (2) a physical-risk rationale for the decision; and (3) a decision status OR portfolio coverage (see coverageRule). measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A portfolio-level decision or defined pathway (relocate/retire/sell/redesign/alter) on material high-risk assets, with a physical-risk rationale and status or coverage.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Site-level physical hardening with no change of ownership/use/location (that is A2); a generic 'we review our portfolio' statement; a decision with no physical-risk rationale; a portfolio claim with no status or coverage.

Our portfolio strategy defines a pathway to retire or repurpose all facilities above our water-stress exposure threshold by 2030, covering 11 assets.
The Board approved relocating our flood-exposed central distribution hub to a lower-risk inland site following the physical-risk review.
We redesigned the use of three heat-exposed assets, converting them from continuous production to buffered operation, across our highest-risk tier.

The company considers a range of factors in portfolio decisions.
We hardened flood defences at one of our plants last year.
Our assets are managed in line with our capital-allocation framework.

measures.title: Critical utility, technology and communications dependencies have resilience controls
measures.definition: Whether the company identifies an alternate supply, redundancy, backup, restoration arrangement, manual workaround or resilience control for a named critical utility, transport, data, technology or communications dependency. NEW measure.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a named critical utility/technology/comms dependency AND a resilience control for it, both quote-verifiable. Boundary: utility/technology/comms continuity CONTROL here; mapping the dependency without a control is U7; a supplier/logistics control is A8. CHANGE: a dependency ASSESSMENT with no control does NOT count here — it belongs in U7. measures.title: Risk financing addresses physical-climate insurability and residual loss
measures.definition: Whether a physical-risk/insurability disclosure addresses at least one insurability/risk-financing element and describes an action, assessment or strategic response. Replaces C4-insurability-strategy.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a named insurability/risk-financing element AND a described action/assessment/strategic response, both quote-verifiable. 'We maintain appropriate insurance' or a bare statement that the company is insured is No. Captive/parametric cover, rising premiums, cover withdrawal, business interruption and uninsured/contingent-liquidity treatment all qualify.
measures.primaryAssessmentTarget: Risk-financing strategy for physical climate impacts
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (physical-risk/insurability attribution required). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a physical-risk/insurability disclosure addressing AT LEAST ONE of — premium or deductible trends, availability/withdrawal of cover, exclusions, self-insurance/captive/parametric cover, business interruption, uninsured exposure or contingent liquidity; and (2) a described ACTION, assessment or strategic response. Boundary: risk FINANCING here; resilience resourcing is A6; appraisal is A7. DEFINITION: a strategic treatment of physical-climate insurability or residual loss with a response — not 'we maintain appropriate insurance'.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A physical-risk/insurability disclosure addressing at least one named element (premiums/deductibles, availability/withdrawal, exclusions, captive/parametric, business interruption, uninsured exposure, contingent liquidity) with a described response.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: 'We maintain appropriate insurance'; a bare statement of being insured; an insurance claim with no physical-risk link or response; resilience resourcing (A6); investment appraisal (A7).

We quantify our uninsured physical-climate exposure and hold a contingent-liquidity facility sized against the modelled residual loss.
Insurers signalled potential cover withdrawal at two coastal sites; our response combines self-insurance, deductible increases and accelerated hardening.
Our risk-financing strategy addresses business-interruption cover limits and the growing share of physical exposure retained on our balance sheet.

The company has comprehensive insurance arrangements in place.

measures.category: Reduce vulnerability and adapt the business
measures.title: Material chronic-hazard effects on water, workforce and productive capacity are managed
measures.definition: Whether a water, heat, smoke, drought or chronic-condition control identifies the exposed business activity/people/site and states an operational threshold, protocol, coverage, action or performance indicator. Replaces C8-water-security and C10-workforce-heat-stress.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a chronic-hazard control, an identified exposed activity/people/site, and a threshold/protocol/coverage/action/KPI, all quote-verifiable. A generic health-and-safety statement, a water-stewardship claim, or a mere mention of heat/drought with no control is No. Applies only where the chronic hazard is material to the company.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK physical_climate (chronic physical-hazard attribution required). APPLICABILITY if_material — applies ONLY if the materiality profile identifies water dependency, outdoor/non-conditioned workforce exposure, heat/smoke exposure, drought exposure or equivalent chronic physical risk; otherwise a non-applicable determination, not an automatic No. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a water, heat, smoke, drought or chronic-condition CONTROL; (2) it identifies the exposed business activity, people or site; and (3) it states an operational threshold, protocol, coverage, action or performance indicator. Boundary: CHRONIC-hazard continuity here; acute hardening is A2; mapping with no control is U-pillar. DEFINITION: a managed response to a material chronic hazard affecting water, workforce or productive capacity — not a generic health-and-safety or water-stewardship statement.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A chronic-hazard (water/heat/smoke/drought) control that names the exposed activity/people/site and states an operational threshold, protocol, coverage, action or performance indicator.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A generic health-and-safety statement; a water-stewardship or water-reduction claim with no continuity link; a bare hazard mention; acute physical hardening (A2); a dependency assessment with no control.
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report describes a heat-stress protocol with wet-bulb thresholds that trigger shift changes for outdoor workers at named sites.
2. A company discloses water-recycling and abstraction limits managing drought exposure at its water-dependent plants, with coverage stated.
3. A disclosure sets a wildfire-smoke air-quality protocol protecting workforce and production at facilities in fire-prone regions.
positiveExamples: Our heat-stress protocol sets wet-bulb thresholds that trigger adjusted shift patterns and rest breaks for outdoor workers at our 12 highest-exposure sites.
We manage drought exposure at our six water-dependent plants through recycling, abstraction limits and on-site storage, covering 100% of at-risk capacity.
A wildfire-smoke air-quality protocol suspends outdoor operations above defined PM2.5 thresholds, protecting workforce and production at fire-prone sites.
Chronic water-stress management includes a site-level water-intensity KPI and a reduction target for our most drought-exposed facilities.
negativeExamples: We are committed to the health and safety of our employees.
The company is a responsible steward of water resources.
We recognise that heat and drought can affect our operations.
Water efficiency is part of our environmental programme.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Generic H&S, water-stewardship, or a bare hazard mention.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A chronic-hazard control naming the exposed activity/people/site with a threshold/protocol/coverage/action/KPI.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a CONTROL for a material chronic hazard (water/heat/smoke/drought) tied to exposed people/sites and a threshold/action — not generic H&S or stewardship?

measures.title: A formal business-continuity management system covers material critical activities
measures.definition: Whether a system, programme or policy has designated ownership, a defined scope covering material business units/critical activities, and a review/maintenance cycle. Replaces part of D1-business-continuity-tested.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a system/programme/policy, designated ownership, a defined material scope, and a review/maintenance cycle, all quote-verifiable. Bare 'we have a business-continuity plan', or one local site emergency plan, is No. Alignment to ISO 22301 with ownership, scope and review is a strong Yes signal.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK operational_resilience (named-disruption-and-control attribution; climate wording NOT required). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a business-continuity SYSTEM, programme or policy; (2) designated OWNERSHIP; (3) a defined SCOPE covering material business units/critical activities (see coverageRule); and (4) a review/maintenance CYCLE. Boundary: the managed SYSTEM here; recovery objectives are P2; crisis command is P3; climate-scenario integration is P4; exercising is P6. DEFINITION: a managed, owned, scoped and maintained BCMS — not the bare existence of 'a BCP' or a single local emergency plan.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A continuity system/programme/policy with designated ownership, a defined scope over material units/critical activities, and a review/maintenance cycle.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: Bare 'we have a BCP'; a single local emergency plan; a continuity claim with no owner, scope or review cycle; recovery objectives alone (P2); a crisis-contact list (P3).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report states a Group BCMS aligned to ISO 22301, owned by the Chief Operating Officer, covering all critical business services and reviewed annually.
2. A disclosure describes a continuity programme with a named owner, a scope defined over its material business units, and a defined maintenance cycle.
3. A company documents a continuity-management policy covering its critical activities with assigned ownership and an annual review.
positiveExamples: Our Group business-continuity management system is aligned to ISO 22301, owned by the COO, covers all critical business services and is reviewed annually.
The continuity programme has a named owner, a scope defined across our eight material business units, and a documented annual maintenance cycle.
We operate a continuity-management policy covering our critical activities, with assigned ownership and a formal review each year.
Our BCMS scope covers 100% of services classified business-critical, under a designated Resilience Director and a defined review calendar.
negativeExamples: We have a business-continuity plan in place.
The company is prepared for operational disruptions.
Each site maintains its own local emergency procedures.
Business continuity is managed as part of our operations.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Bare 'a BCP', a single local plan, or no owner/scope/review.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: An owned, scoped, maintained BCMS covering material critical activities.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a MANAGED system (owner + material scope + review cycle) — not just the existence of a plan?
