measures.title: Continuity strategies and measurable recovery objectives are defined for critical activities
measures.definition: Whether a continuity arrangement sets recovery strategies and recovery objectives for critical activities, systems, people, facilities or third parties. Replaces part of D1-business-continuity-tested.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires both a recovery strategy and at least one measurable recovery objective (RTO/RPO/MTD/service-level/alternative capacity/restoration target), quote-verifiable. A plan with no recovery objective, or a vague 'we will restore operations' with no metric, is No. The objective must be measurable, not aspirational.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK operational_resilience (named-disruption-and-control attribution). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a continuity arrangement that sets RECOVERY STRATEGIES; and (2) measurable RECOVERY OBJECTIVES for critical activities, systems, people, facilities or third parties — qualifying metrics include RTO, RPO, maximum tolerable downtime, a service-level threshold, alternative capacity or a restoration target. Boundary: the actionable DESIGN (strategies + objectives) here; the managing system is P1; exercising is P6. DEFINITION: a continuity design with usable recovery strategies AND at least one measurable recovery objective — not a plan with no recovery objective.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A continuity design with recovery strategies AND at least one measurable recovery objective (RTO, RPO, maximum tolerable downtime, service-level threshold, alternative capacity, restoration target).
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A plan with no recovery objective; a vague 'we will restore operations quickly'; a continuity system with no strategy/metric (that is P1); an exercise record (P6).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure sets RTOs and RPOs for each critical system plus alternative-site recovery strategies.
2. A company defines maximum tolerable downtime per critical activity and the recovery strategy (workaround, alternate capacity) that meets it.
3. A report states service-level restoration targets and the continuity strategies designed to achieve them for its critical services.
positiveExamples: We define RTOs and RPOs for every critical system and maintain alternative-site recovery strategies to meet them.
Each critical activity has a maximum tolerable downtime and a documented recovery strategy — workaround or alternate capacity — designed to meet it.
Our continuity design sets service-level restoration targets for critical services and the specific strategies that deliver them.
Recovery objectives (RTO 4 hours, RPO 15 minutes) are defined for core transaction processing, with failover capacity sized accordingly.
negativeExamples: We aim to restore operations as quickly as possible after any disruption.
Our business-continuity plan covers recovery of critical functions.
The company is committed to operational resilience.
We have procedures to recover from incidents.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A plan with no recovery objective or metric.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: Recovery strategies plus at least one measurable recovery objective for critical activities.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a measurable recovery objective (RTO/RPO/MTD/service target) AND a strategy to meet it — not just 'restore quickly'?

measures.title: Crisis and incident management provides defined command and communication arrangements
measures.definition: Whether a disclosure assigns incident roles/authority, describes a crisis-command or escalation structure, and names at least one stakeholder-communication route relevant to a disruption. NEW measure.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires assigned roles/authority, a command/escalation structure, and a named stakeholder-communication route, all quote-verifiable. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) assigned incident ROLES/authority; (2) a described crisis-command or escalation STRUCTURE; and (3) at least one named stakeholder-COMMUNICATION route (employees, customers, suppliers, regulators, communities or investors) relevant to a disruption. Boundary: crisis COMMAND + communication here; the continuity system is P1; recovery objectives are P2; pre-event triggers are P5. DEFINITION: a defined crisis-management structure with roles, command/escalation and a stakeholder-communication route — not an emergency phone number or a generic crisis-policy claim.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: An assigned-role/authority crisis structure with a command/escalation arrangement and at least one named stakeholder-communication route for a disruption.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: An emergency contact number; a generic crisis-management-policy claim; a continuity system with no crisis structure (P1); a plan with no communication route; media-relations boilerplate.
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report describes a crisis-management team with defined roles and decision authority, an escalation structure, and defined communication routes to employees, customers and regulators.
2. A disclosure sets out an incident-command structure with tiered escalation and a stakeholder-communication plan for major disruptions.
3. A company documents crisis roles, an activation/escalation protocol, and how it communicates with investors and customers during an incident.

We operate an incident-command structure with clear escalation tiers and a stakeholder-communication plan covering staff, suppliers and investors.
Crisis roles and an activation/escalation protocol are documented, together with how we communicate with customers and regulators during a disruption.
Our Gold-Silver-Bronze command structure assigns authority at each tier and defines internal and external communication responsibilities.
negativeExamples: In an emergency, staff should call the incident hotline.
The company has a crisis-management policy.
We are prepared to respond to incidents as they arise.
Our communications team handles media enquiries.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: An emergency number or generic crisis-policy claim.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A crisis structure with roles/authority, command/escalation, and a named stakeholder-communication route.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Are crisis roles/authority, a command/escalation structure, AND a stakeholder-communication route all present — not just a policy or hotline?

ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a continuity/emergency-response/disaster-recovery/crisis-management plan; (2) it EXPLICITLY covers a material physical hazard, weather/natural-disaster scenario or physical climate impact; and (3) it states a corresponding control, activation or recovery approach. Boundary: the CLIMATE INTEGRATION in continuity here; a generic BCMS is P1; a physical-risk disclosure NOT connected to continuity is U-pillar; pre-event triggers are P5. DEFINITION: continuity planning that is explicitly connected to a material physical-climate scenario with a response — the bridge between physical risk and operational continuity. Our crisis plan integrates wildfire and water-curtailment scenarios for exposed facilities, with a defined control and activation step for each.

The company assesses physical climate risks across its sites.
We are prepared for a range of operational disruptions.
Natural disasters are considered in our risk management.

measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a disclosed exercise/test, an identified scope/scenario, AND a recorded outcome/finding/corrective action, all quote-verifiable. A promise to test, a generic 'we conduct exercises', a training event with no test scope, or a test with no result/follow-up is No.

measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A disclosed exercise/test with an identified population/scenario/scope AND a recorded outcome, finding, corrective action or change.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A promise to test; a generic 'we run exercises'; a training event with no test scope; a test with no result or follow-up; actual event recovery performance (R1); cross-event learning (L2).

measures.title: Actual recovery performance after material disruption is disclosed against an objective or service threshold
measures.definition: Whether a named event is linked to a recovery metric or service/operating result and compared with a stated target, threshold, expected service level or objectively bounded recovery outcome. Replaces D3-recovery-performance.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a named event, a recovery metric/result, AND a comparison to a target/threshold/service level, all quote-verifiable. An RTO target with no event performance, or anecdotal 'operations resumed quickly', is No. If NO qualifying event occurred in the period, treat as non-applicable (exclude), not No.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK performance (event_or_exercise attribution required). APPLICABILITY if_event_occurred — applies ONLY when the company has experienced a material/disclosed disruption in the measurement period; ABSENCE of a qualifying event is an applicability determination, NOT an automatic No. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a NAMED event; (2) linked to a recovery metric or service/operating result; and (3) COMPARED with a stated target, threshold, expected service level or objectively bounded recovery outcome. Boundary: actual recovery PERFORMANCE here; an RTO target with no event is P2; impact quantification is R2; learning is L2. DEFINITION: evidence that an actual disruption was recovered against an objective — not an RTO target without event performance, and not anecdotal 'operations resumed quickly'.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A named disruption linked to a recovery metric/service result AND compared with a stated target, threshold, expected service level or bounded recovery outcome.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: An RTO/RPO target with no actual event performance (that is P2); anecdotal 'operations resumed quickly'; an impact figure with no recovery comparison (R2); no qualifying event in the period (non-applicable, not No).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report states that after the June flood, the affected site was restored within 18 hours against a 24-hour RTO.
2. A company discloses that following a hurricane, service was recovered to 95% within two days, meeting its service-level target.
3. A disclosure links a named power-loss event to the time taken to restore critical systems, compared with the recovery objective.
positiveExamples: Following the June flood at our Midlands site, operations were restored within 18 hours against our 24-hour recovery-time objective.
After Hurricane X, we recovered service to 95% of normal within two days, meeting our stated service-level recovery target.
The December grid-outage event was contained with critical systems restored in 3 hours, inside the 4-hour RTO.
Our main plant resumed full output nine days after the storm, ahead of the 14-day recovery objective set in our continuity plan.
negativeExamples: We aim to recover operations within our target recovery times.
The company recovered quickly from recent disruptions.
Our recovery-time objective for critical systems is four hours.
Operations resumed promptly after the incident.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: An RTO target with no event, or anecdotal quick recovery.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A named event recovered and measured against a stated objective/threshold.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is an actual event's recovery measured AGAINST a stated target/service level — not just a target or an anecdote?

measures.title: Operational and financial impacts of material disruptions are measured and disclosed
measures.definition: Whether the company quantifies one or more relevant effects of a material disruption and identifies the event or reporting period to which it relates. Replaces E1-incident-loss-metrics and the historic-event portion of B6-financial-impact.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a quantified impact AND an identified event/period, both quote-verifiable. Do NOT require an improving trend. A forward-looking impact estimate (that is U4), or an unquantified 'the storm affected operations', is No. If no qualifying event/metric, treat as non-applicable.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK performance (event_or_exercise attribution required). APPLICABILITY if_event_occurred — applies when a material/disclosed disruption occurs OR when the company reports a relevant incident metric. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) the company QUANTIFIES one or more relevant effects — downtime, lost production/service, revenue/EBITDA/cash-flow impact, business interruption, repair cost, customer impact, insurance recovery or similar; and (2) it IDENTIFIES the event or reporting period to which it relates. CHANGE FROM LEGACY: do NOT require an improving trend — a worse hazard year or better reporting does not demonstrate weaker management by itself. Boundary: impact QUANTIFICATION here; recovery-vs-target is R1; forward-looking modelling is U4. DEFINITION: measured impact of an actual disruption tied to the event/period — not a forward estimate and not an unquantified mention.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A quantified operational/financial impact (downtime, lost production/service, revenue/EBITDA/cash-flow, business interruption, repair cost, customer impact, insurance recovery) tied to a named event or reporting period.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A forward-looking impact estimate (that is U4); an unquantified 'the storm affected us'; recovery time vs target (R1); a demand for an improving trend (removed); no qualifying event/metric (non-applicable).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report quantifies 12 days of lost production and GBP 8m business-interruption cost from a named flood event.
2. A company discloses the revenue and repair-cost impact of a hurricane in the reporting period.
3. A disclosure reports downtime hours and insured/uninsured loss from a named power-outage incident.
positiveExamples: The June flood caused 12 days of lost production and GBP 8m of business-interruption cost, net of GBP 5m insurance recovery.
Hurricane X reduced quarterly revenue by GBP 15m and incurred GBP 6m of repair cost, as disclosed for the reporting period.
A regional power outage caused 36 hours of downtime at two sites, with GBP 2.1m uninsured loss in the year.
Severe heat in 2025 cut output by 7% at our affected plants, quantified as GBP 4m lost contribution.
negativeExamples: Extreme weather affected our operations during the year.
We experienced some disruption from a storm event.
The company may face financial impacts from physical climate risks.
Climate events could cost us up to GBP 50m by 2030.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A forward estimate, an unquantified mention, or no event.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A quantified impact of an actual disruption tied to a named event/period.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is an ACTUAL event's impact quantified and tied to the event/period — not a forward projection or a vague mention?

measures.title: Resilience performance or residual physical-climate exposure is monitored against a dated target or risk tolerance
measures.definition: Whether a quantified and dated resilience target, residual-risk limit or risk-tolerance metric has a baseline/denominator and reported progress, current result or variance. Replaces E2-targets-progress; absorbs B7-gross-residual-exposure as supporting evidence.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a quantified+dated target/limit/tolerance, a baseline/denominator, AND reported progress/current result/variance, all quote-verifiable. A broad ambition, a one-off exposure figure with no target, or a target with no progress/current status is No. Gross-vs-residual exposed value qualifies where relevant but is not required.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK performance (event_or_exercise/monitoring attribution). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a QUANTIFIED and DATED resilience target, residual-risk limit or risk-tolerance metric; (2) a BASELINE or denominator; and (3) reported PROGRESS, current result or variance. Boundary: ongoing monitoring/targets here; one-off exposure numbers belong in U-pillar; closed-loop learning is L2. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (spec): gross-versus-residual exposed value remains a strong qualifying metric for L1 where relevant, but it is NOT a universal standalone measure of management effectiveness. DEFINITION: a dated, quantified target or risk-tolerance metric with a baseline and current progress — not a broad ambition, a one-off exposure number, or a target with no progress/status.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A quantified, dated resilience target / residual-risk limit / risk-tolerance metric with a baseline or denominator AND reported progress, current result or variance.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A broad resilience ambition with no metric; a one-off exposure number with no target (U-pillar); a target with no baseline or no current progress; closed-loop learning (L2).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report sets a dated target to reduce residual flood-exposed value by 40% by 2028 from a 2023 baseline, and reports current progress.
2. A company discloses a risk-tolerance limit for business-interruption exposure and its current position against that limit.
3. A disclosure tracks a resilience KPI (e.g. % critical sites hardened) against a dated target with year-on-year progress.
positiveExamples: We target a 40% reduction in residual flood-exposed asset value by 2028 from a 2023 baseline, and report 22% achieved to date.
Our risk-tolerance limit for annual business-interruption exposure is GBP 20m; we are currently within tolerance at GBP 14m.
We track the percentage of critical sites meeting our resilience standard against a dated target, reporting 68% versus an 80% 2026 goal.
Gross-versus-residual exposed value is monitored against a residual-risk ceiling, with current-year variance disclosed.
negativeExamples: We aim to improve the resilience of our business over time.
Our total climate-exposed asset value is GBP 1.2bn.
The company is committed to reducing its physical risk.
We have set ambitious resilience goals.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A broad ambition, a one-off exposure number, or a target with no progress.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A quantified+dated target/tolerance with a baseline and reported progress/current status.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is there a dated quantified target/tolerance WITH a baseline AND current progress/variance — not an ambition or single number?

measures.title: Lessons from events, near misses and exercises are assigned and implemented
measures.definition: Whether a named event, near miss or exercise produces a documented lesson/finding, a resulting action/change is assigned or described, and completion/status is evidenced. Replaces E3-post-event-learning.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a named event/near-miss/exercise, a documented lesson, an assigned/described resulting change, AND completion/status, all quote-verifiable. A generic continuous-improvement statement, or a 'lessons were learned' claim with no change/status, is No. Near misses and exercises count — do not require an actual disaster.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK performance (event_or_exercise attribution required). APPLICABILITY always (companies can learn from near misses and exercises, so absence of a recent disaster is not a penalty). ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a NAMED event, near miss or exercise produces a documented LESSON/finding; (2) a resulting ACTION/change is assigned or described; and (3) COMPLETION/status is evidenced. Boundary: CLOSED-LOOP learning here; the exercise itself is P6; recovery performance is R1; target monitoring is L1. DEFINITION: a documented lesson from an event/near-miss/exercise that led to an assigned, status-evidenced change — not a generic continuous-improvement statement or a lessons-learned claim without a change.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A named event/near-miss/exercise producing a documented lesson, an assigned or described resulting action/change, AND evidenced completion/status.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A generic continuous-improvement statement; a 'lessons learned' claim with no change; the exercise record itself with no learning loop (P6); recovery performance (R1); target monitoring (L1).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A report states a post-flood review produced findings, assigned remediation actions, and confirms their completion status.
2. A company discloses that a near-miss power event led to a defined control change, owned and tracked to closure.
3. A disclosure describes lessons from a continuity exercise, the plan changes made, and their implementation status.
positiveExamples: Our post-flood review produced specific findings; remediation actions were assigned to owners and all were confirmed complete within six months.
A near-miss grid event led us to add a documented control change, owned by site engineering and tracked to closure.
Lessons from our 2025 continuity exercise drove four plan changes, each assigned and now implemented.
Following a supplier near-miss, we revised our dual-sourcing standard; the change is recorded as completed and audited.
negativeExamples: We are committed to continuous improvement.
We learn from incidents and apply the lessons.
The company takes a proactive approach to improvement.
Lessons learned are shared across the organisation.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: Generic continuous-improvement or a lessons claim with no change/status.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A documented lesson from an event/near-miss/exercise with an assigned, status-evidenced change.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Did a named event/near-miss/exercise lead to an ASSIGNED change with evidenced completion — not a generic improvement claim?

measures.title: Physical-risk and continuity assumptions are periodically reassessed after material change
measures.definition: Whether the company states a review/reassessment trigger or cycle that applies after material changes and indicates the resilience/continuity programme is updated as a result. NEW measure.
measures.scoringGuidance: Binary. Yes requires a reassessment trigger/cycle tied to material change AND evidence the programme is updated as a result, both quote-verifiable. A fixed policy review with no relation to the risk/control environment is No. Triggers may be footprint/asset change, supplier change, insurance availability, new climate science/data, or disruptive events.
measures.substantiveDefinition: TRACK performance (reassessment/currency attribution). APPLICABILITY always. ATOMIC PREDICATES, all required: (1) a stated review/reassessment TRIGGER or cycle that applies after MATERIAL CHANGES in footprint, assets, suppliers, insurance/availability, climate science, risk data or disruptive events; and (2) an indication that the resilience/continuity programme is UPDATED as a result. Boundary: programme CURRENCY (keeping assumptions live) here; the system itself is P1; target monitoring is L1; closed-loop event learning is L2. DEFINITION: a reassessment mechanism tied to the risk/control environment that keeps the programme current — not a fixed-calendar policy review unrelated to change.
measures.whatConstitutesEvidence: A review/reassessment trigger or cycle tied to material change (footprint, assets, suppliers, insurance, climate science, risk data, events) WITH an indication the programme is updated as a result.
measures.whatDoesNotConstituteEvidence: A fixed-calendar policy review with no link to the risk/control environment; a generic 'we review our policies annually'; the continuity system (P1); target monitoring (L1); event learning (L2).
measures.fallbackYesCriterion:
1. A disclosure states physical-risk and continuity assumptions are reassessed whenever the company acquires assets, changes suppliers or new climate science emerges, and the programme is updated accordingly.
2. A company describes a trigger-based review tied to insurance-availability change and disruptive events, with resulting programme updates.
3. A report states that after any material footprint change, the resilience programme and its assumptions are re-evaluated and revised.
positiveExamples: Physical-risk and continuity assumptions are reassessed whenever we acquire assets, change critical suppliers, or new climate science emerges, and the programme is updated accordingly.
Our trigger-based review is tied to changes in insurance availability and to disruptive events, each prompting a documented programme update.
After any material change to our footprint, the resilience programme and its underlying assumptions are re-evaluated and revised.
New regional climate data triggers a reassessment of exposure assumptions and a refresh of the affected continuity plans.
negativeExamples: We review our policies on a regular basis.
The company keeps its risk-management framework under review.
Our continuity plans are reviewed annually.
We update our procedures from time to time.

c1AchievementGuidance.no_cases: A fixed-calendar review unrelated to the risk/control environment.
c1AchievementGuidance.yes_cases: A reassessment trigger/cycle tied to material change with the programme updated as a result.
c1AchievementGuidance.distinguishing_test: Is reassessment triggered by MATERIAL CHANGE (footprint/suppliers/science/events) AND does the programme get updated — not just a periodic policy review?
